title: Caucasian Albania
capsule: Caucasian Albania was an ancient kingdom occupying roughly modern Azerbaijan and parts of Dagestan, first attested in classical sources around the 1st century BCE and known to Greek and Roman geographers as a land of multiple languages and tribes. The kingdom was a buffer between Rome and Parthia, and later between Byzantium and Sasanian Persia; its Arsacid dynasty converted to Christianity in the early 4th century CE. Repeated Sasanian pressure reduced it to a tributary kingdom by the 3rd–4th century CE; Arab conquest in the 7th century brought it under the Umayyad Caliphate, extinguishing the Caucasian Albanian state by around 510 in its original form.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial extent is only approximately known from classical geographers (Strabo, Ptolemy) and Armenian chronicles; internal administrative boundaries are essentially undocumented and modern maps represent scholarly inference.
